label: DNA Methylation
description: DNA methylation is one of the three best-studied epigenetic mechanisms, involving addition of methyl groups to cytosines at CpG dinucleotides.

label: Epigenetics
description: DNA methylation is one of the three best-studied epigenetic mechanisms, involving addition of methyl groups to cytosines at CpG dinucleotides.

label: Histone Modification
description: Histone modification — covalent marks on histone tails including acetylation, methylation, phosphorylation, ubiquitination — is a core epigenetic mechanism.

label: Non-Coding RNA
description: Non-coding RNAs such as MicroRNA and piRNAs regulate gene expression transcriptionally and post-transcriptionally as an epigenetic mechanism.

label: DNA Methyltransferase
description: The process of DNA methylation is catalyzed by a family of enzymes called DNA Methyltransferases (DNMTs).

label: DNMT1
description: DNMT1 is the primary enzyme responsible for maintaining DNA methylation patterns during DNA Replication, copying the methylation pattern of the parental strand onto the daughter strand.

label: UHRF1
description: During S Phase, DNMT1 is recruited to replication foci through its interaction with UHRF1, which recognizes hemi-methylated CpG sites via its SRA domain.

label: SAM
description: DNMT1 transfers a methyl group from S-adenosylmethionine (SAM) to the C5 position of cytosine on the nascent strand.

label: DNMT3a
description: DNMT3a is a de novo methyltransferase responsible for establishing new DNA methylation patterns at previously unmethylated DNA.

label: DNMT3b
description: DNMT3a forms complexes with its paralog DNMT3b and with the accessory protein DNMT3L to deposit methylation at targeted loci.

label: Gene Bodies
description: DNMT3a exhibits a preference for gene bodies and intergenic regions, in contrast to DNMT3b which favors repetitive elements.

label: Hematopoiesis
description: DNMT3a remains crucial for hematopoiesis — especially hematopoietic stem cell differentiation and self-renewal.

label: Clonal Hematopoiesis
description: Somatic mutations in DNMT3A are among the most common drivers of clonal hematopoiesis of indeterminate potential (CHIP).

label: Acute Myeloid Leukemia
description: Recurrent DNMT3A mutations (notably R882H) are found in ~20% of acute myeloid leukemia (AML) cases.

label: Pericentromeric Satellite Repeats
description: DNMT3b exhibits a strong preference for pericentromeric satellite repeats and other repetitive DNA, depositing methylation essential for heterochromatin formation.

label: ICF Syndrome
description: Mutations in the DNMT3B gene are the cause of ICF Syndrome (Immunodeficiency, Centromere instability, and Facial anomalies).

label: Gene Silencing
description: High levels of methylation in promoter regions, often concentrated in CpG Islands, are strongly associated with gene silencing.

label: Chromatin Remodeling
description: Methylated DNA is recognized by MBD proteins that recruit chromatin remodeling factors and histone deacetylases, leading to condensed transcriptionally inactive chromatin.

label: Epigenetic Clock
description: Epigenetic clocks are built from DNA methylation measurements at defined CpG sites whose methylation changes predictably with age.

label: Transposable Elements
description: DNA methylation helps repress potentially harmful repetitive elements and retrotransposons within the genome.

label: Histone Acetyltransferase
description: Histone Acetyltransferase (HAT) transfers an acetyl group from acetyl-CoA to specific lysine residues on histone tails, a key component of epigenetic regulation.

label: Histone Acetylation
description: Histone Acetyltransferase (HAT) transfers an acetyl group from acetyl-CoA to specific lysine residues on histone tails, a key component of epigenetic regulation.

label: Histone Deacetylase
description: HATs act in dynamic opposition to HDACs; signal-dependent recruitment of HATs couples extracellular cues to gene activation.

label: Euchromatin
description: Acetylation neutralizes the positive charge of histone tails, transitioning chromatin from condensed to open, transcriptionally active euchromatin.

label: Acetyl-CoA
description: HATs transfer an acetyl group from acetyl-CoA to specific lysine residues on histone tails.

label: Deacetylation
description: HDACs remove acetyl groups from ε-N-acetyl-lysine residues on histones, allowing chromatin to wrap DNA more tightly and generally repressing transcription.

label: Heterochromatin
description: By removing acetyl groups, HDACs restore positive charge of lysine side chains, strengthening interaction with DNA and leading to more condensed heterochromatin.

label: Sirtuins
description: Class III HDACs are the Sirtuins (SIRT1–7), NAD+-dependent deacetylases that link metabolic state to chromatin regulation.

label: Deacetylases
description: Sirtuins are NAD+-dependent deacetylases that link metabolic state to chromatin regulation and are strongly implicated in aging and longevity.

label: Yeast
description: Overexpression of Sir2 extends lifespan in yeast by preventing the formation of toxic rDNA circles.

label: H4K16
description: Sir2/SIRT1 is an H4K16 deacetylase required for silencing and chromatin compaction at mating type loci, rDNA, and telomeres.

label: LINE-1
description: SIRT6 is enriched at LINE-1 5'UTR loci and mono-ADP ribosylates KAP1, promoting heterochromatinization of L1 elements.

label: HAT
description: HAT is the common abbreviation for Histone Acetyltransferase.

label: HDAC
description: HDAC stands for Histone Deacetylase.

label: Biological Age
description: An epigenetic clock is a statistical estimator of biological age built from DNA methylation measurements at a defined set of CpG sites.

label: DNAmGrimAge
description: DNAmGrimAge is a second-generation epigenetic clock trained to predict morbidity, mortality, and physiological decline rather than time.

label: Partial Reprogramming
description: Partial cellular reprogramming has shown measurable epigenetic clock reversal, motivating use of clocks as endpoints in rejuvenation trials.

label: Epigenetic Drift
description: The best-characterized signature of epigenetic drift is global hypomethylation of repetitive elements and gene bodies coupled with site-specific hypermethylation of gene promoters.

label: Global Hypomethylation
description: The best-characterized signature of epigenetic drift is global hypomethylation of repetitive elements and gene bodies coupled with site-specific hypermethylation of gene promoters.

label: Yamanaka Factors
description: The Yamanaka Factors (OSKM: Oct4, Sox2, Klf4, c-Myc) are used to induce pluripotency in differentiated Somatic Cells.

label: Somatic Cells
description: The Yamanaka Factors (OSKM: Oct4, Sox2, Klf4, c-Myc) are used to induce pluripotency in differentiated Somatic Cells.

label: Induced Pluripotent Stem Cells
description: The four Yamanaka Factors revert fibroblasts to an embryonic-stem-cell-like state, generating iPSCs.

label: Klf4
description: The Yamanaka Factors comprise Oct4, Sox2, Klf4, and c-Myc.

label: c-Myc
description: The Yamanaka Factors comprise Oct4, Sox2, Klf4, and c-Myc.

label: OSKM
description: The Yamanaka Factors are also known as the OSKM cassette (Oct4, Sox2, Klf4, c-Myc).

label: Pluripotency
description: Oct4 is a definitive marker and master regulator of pluripotency, essential for self-renewal of undifferentiated ES cells and iPSCs.

label: Mesenchymal-to-Epithelial Transition
description: During Cellular Reprogramming, Oct4 initiates the mesenchymal-to-epithelial transition and resets the epigenome.

label: H3K9me3
description: During reprogramming, H3K9me3/H3K27me3 repressive marks are erased at Oct4 target loci.

label: Neural Stem Cell
description: Sox2 maintains Neural Stem Cell identity in the adult SVZ/SGZ and is required for tissue homeostasis in multiple epithelia.

label: Snail
description: Klf4 opposes the EMT drivers Snail and Slug, sitting at the polarity between epithelial identity and mesenchymal dispersal.

label: Slug
description: Klf4 opposes the EMT drivers Snail and Slug during reprogramming.

label: Cellular Reprogramming
description: Cellular Reprogramming is fundamentally an epigenetic remodeling process that erases somatic memory and installs a new identity.

label: Epigenetic Remodeling
description: Cellular Reprogramming is fundamentally an epigenetic remodeling process that erases somatic memory and installs a new identity.

label: Teratoma
description: Partial reprogramming contrasts with full reprogramming to iPSCs, which risks teratoma formation.

label: Rejuvenation
description: The dominant experimental strategy for rejuvenation is Cellular Reprogramming with the Yamanaka Factors (OSKM).

label: Quiescence
description: Quiescence is a state of reversible proliferative arrest in which cells exit the Cell Cycle but retain the capacity to re-enter upon appropriate stimuli.

label: Cell Cycle Arrest
description: Quiescence is a state of reversible proliferative arrest in which cells exit the Cell Cycle but retain the capacity to re-enter upon appropriate stimuli.

label: Retinoblastoma Protein
description: Quiescence is enforced at the Restriction Point by the Retinoblastoma Protein (pRb), which sequesters E2F transcription factors and blocks S-phase genes.

label: Hematopoietic Stem Cell
description: Adult stem cells such as Hematopoietic Stem Cells spend most of their lives in quiescence to protect the genome and preserve self-renewal.

label: RB1
description: RB1 (product of the Retinoblastoma gene) sequesters E2F transcription factors and blocks S-phase genes to enforce quiescence.

label: DNA Damage Response
description: Senescence in adult tissues can be triggered by a persistent DNA damage response (DDR) induced by various internal and external factors.

label: cGAS-STING Pathway
description: Cytoplasmic chromatin fragments detected by cGAS activate the cGAS-STING-NF-κB pathways to induce SASP expression.

label: Cytoplasmic Chromatin Fragments
description: Senescent cells release damaged DNA into the cytoplasm forming CCF, which is detected by cGAS, activating STING and NF-κB.

label: DNA Hypomethylation
description: Age-related DNA demethylation and heterochromatin decompaction activate LINE-1 retrotransposons, triggering cGAS-STING inflammation.

label: HERV
source_file: src/notes/epigenetics/_document_ - The role of the dynamic epigenetic landscape in senescence_orchestrating SASP expression.md
description: HERV RNA undergoes reverse transcription in senescent cells, triggering cGAS/STING-dependent upregulation of SASP factors.

label: H3K27me3
description: Depleting or inhibiting EZH2 leads to removal of H3K27me3 from SASP loci, enabling derepression of SASP genes.

label: EZH2
description: EZH2 is the histone methyltransferase responsible for H3K27me3; its depletion removes H3K27me3 from SASP loci.

label: KDM4
description: KDM4 (JMJD2) is the histone demethylase enzyme targeting H3K9; its expression increases in senescent cells, diminishing H3K9 methylation and enhancing SASP.

label: SUV39H1
description: SUV39H1 is a histone methyltransferase that specifically trimethylates H3K9; it decreases in senescent cells.

label: AP-1
description: The transcription factor AP-1 acts as a pioneering factor that binds to enhancers associated with SASP genes, initiating opening of closed chromatin.

label: H3K27ac
description: BRD4 is an epigenetic reader recognizing H3K27ac at senescence-activated super-enhancers, facilitating SASP gene expression.

label: HDAC4
description: HDAC4 is recruited to H3K27ac loci to monitor the acetylation status of H3K27 at AP-1 regulated super-enhancers.

label: Senescence-Associated Heterochromatin Foci
description: SAHFs are characterized by increased HP1, H3K9me3 marks, macroH2A and HMGA protein binding.

label: macroH2A
description: macroH2A is abundant in SAHF where it promotes transcriptional silencing.

label: H3.3
description: In senescent cells, H3.3 accumulates and progressively replaces canonical H3.1 and H3.2, and both H3.3 and its cleaved product H3.3cs1 trigger senescence when ectopically expressed.

label: H2A.J
description: H2A.J is enriched in SASP promoters, facilitating changes in chromatin accessibility that induce SASP expression.

label: γ-H2A.X
source_file: src/notes/epigenetics/_document_ - The role of the dynamic epigenetic landscape in senescence_orchestrating SASP expression.md
description: γ-H2A.X serves as a beacon to recruit DNA repair proteins at the sites of double-stranded DNA breaks.

label: DNA Repair
description: γ-H2A.X serves as a beacon to recruit DNA repair proteins at the sites of double-stranded DNA breaks.

label: Nucleosome Remodeling
description: During yeast aging, nucleosome occupancy decreases by up to 50% across the genome and half of core histone proteins are lost.

label: SAHF
description: SAHF disruption correlates with reduced SASP expression, though whether SAHF is necessary for SASP remains unresolved.

label: rDNA
description: Sirtuins stabilize human rDNA by recruiting DNMT1, preventing cellular senescence — essentially the same function as yeast Sir2.

label: Disease Modeling
description: iPSCs have transformed Disease Modeling for genetic disorders by generating isogenic neuronal models from patient fibroblasts.

label: Shinya Yamanaka
description: iPSC technology was pioneered by Shinya Yamanaka and colleagues in 2006, who demonstrated that four factors could revert fibroblasts to pluripotency.

label: 5-Azacytidine
description: 5-Azacytidine is a DNA methyltransferase inhibitor that targets DNMT1.

label: Epigenetic Modifiers
description: 5-Azacytidine is classified among epigenetic modifiers as a DNMT inhibitor.

label: Decitabine
description: Decitabine is a DNA methyltransferase inhibitor used in epigenetic therapy.

label: Sodium Valproate
description: Sodium Valproate is a broadly used HDAC-inhibiting anticonvulsant.

label: Trichostatin A
description: Trichostatin A is a histone deacetylase inhibitor used in senescence research.

label: Epigenome
description: Unlike the largely static genome, the Epigenome is dynamic and responsive to diet, stress, exercise, toxins, and social environment.

label: Environment

label: Polycomb Group Proteins
description: During aging, DNA methylation at specific Polycomb group protein target genes is altered, perhaps explaining H3K27 trimethylation changes.

label: Hutchinson-Gilford Progeria Syndrome
description: Hutchinson-Gilford Progeria Syndrome is caused by a truncated form of lamin A, resulting in reduction of heterochromatin.

label: Lamin A
description: Hutchinson-Gilford Progeria Syndrome is caused by a truncated form of lamin A, resulting in reduction of heterochromatin.

label: Werner Syndrome
description: Werner syndrome progeria patients have defective DNA repair with decreased H3K9me3 and SUV39H1 levels.

label: Chromatin
description: The basic unit of chromatin is the nucleosome, made up of 147 DNA base pairs wrapped around an octamer of histone proteins.

label: Nucleosome
description: The basic unit of chromatin is the nucleosome, made up of 147 DNA base pairs wrapped around an octamer of histone proteins.

label: Histone
description: Nucleosomes are made up of an octamer of histone proteins: two copies each of H2A, H2B, H3, and H4.

label: Drug Discovery
description: iPSCs power Drug Discovery through toxicity screening and phenotype-based assays.

label: Regenerative Medicine
description: iPSCs enable Regenerative Medicine applications such as retinal pigment epithelium grafts and cardiomyocyte patches.

label: CRISPR
description: CRISPR-based locus activation is one method for achieving cellular reprogramming beyond transcription-factor delivery.

label: Epithelial-to-Mesenchymal Transition
description: Klf4 cooperates with MET during reprogramming, opposing EMT drivers Snail and Slug.

label: Senolytic Drugs
description: Senolytics involve eliminating senescent cells through targeted drug interventions or immunotherapy.

label: NRTI

label: BRAF
description: In the OIS model, an activated oncogene (typically RAS or BRAF) is ectopically expressed, triggering senescence.

label: Oncogene-Induced Senescence
description: In the OIS model, an activated oncogene (typically RAS or BRAF) is ectopically expressed, triggering senescence.

label: Doxorubicin
description: DNA-damaging chemicals and chemotherapeutic drugs such as Doxorubicin can trigger therapy-induced senescence.

label: Etoposide
description: Etoposide and other DNA-damaging drugs trigger therapy-induced senescence in normal fibroblast or tumor cells.

label: N6-methyladenosine
description: METTL3-METTL14 complex catalyzes N6-methyladenosine (m6A) methylation in mammalian nuclear RNAs.

label: HMGB2
description: In OIS, chromatin-bound HMGB2 binds to SASP gene loci, protecting against spread of repressive heterochromatin and preventing SASP silencing.

label: Topologically Associating Domain
description: Chromatin is arranged into spatial domains known as topologically associated domains (TADs) where DNA sequences interact more frequently.

label: Enhancer-Promoter Looping
description: TADs regulate gene expression by enabling enhancer-promoter looping within the same TAD.

label: MicroRNA
description: In C. elegans, most microRNAs are downregulated with age, and this is reversed by caloric restriction.

label: Dicer
description: Levels of the miRNA processing enzyme Dicer decrease in worms and mice with age, contributing to reduced ncRNAs.

label: H19

label: XIST

label: CXCL5

label: Hydroxychloroquine

label: p62

label: TRIAD

label: Pin1

label: PTPN5

label: K-RAS

label: CDK5

label: Trehalose

label: Celastrol
description: Celastrol activates TFEB via inhibiting mTORC1, reducing insoluble phosphorylated Tau aggregates and improving memory deficiency in Alzheimer's disease models.

label: Bleomycin
description: Bleomycin induces premature senescence via DNA breaks, activating p53-p21 and p16 pathways with SASP secretion.

label: Sodium Butyrate

label: PLK3
description: PLK3 phosphorylates BCL-XL at Ser49, causing cell cycle G2 arrest in lymphoma cells.

label: RSK
